A.explanation: 15 J is the area of the rectangle, which is the net work for the whole cycle, not the work for the compression stage alone.

B.explanation: 25 J does not match $p\Delta V$ for either horizontal stage using $1.0 \times 10^{5} \text{Pa}$ or $1.5 \times 10^{5} \text{Pa}$ with $3.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{m}^{3}$.

C.explanation: Compression at constant $1.0 \times 10^{5} \text{Pa}$ from $5 \times 10^{-4} \text{m}^{3}$ to $2 \times 10^{-4} \text{m}^{3}$ gives $1.0 \times 10^{5} \times 3.0 \times 10^{-4} = 30 \text{ J}$ done on the gas.

D.explanation: 45 J is the work done by the gas during expansion at $1.5 \times 10^{5} \text{Pa}$, not the work done on the gas during compression.

hints: Notice which sides of the pressure-volume rectangle are vertical at $2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$ and $5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$ and which are horizontal at $1.0 \times 10^{5} \text{ Pa}$ and $1.5 \times 10^{5} \text{ Pa}$.
Recall that no work is done when volume is constant, work is done by the gas when volume increases, and work is done on the gas when volume decreases.
For the horizontal stage where volume decreases, use $W = p\Delta V$ with the lower constant pressure and the volume change $3.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$.
walkthrough: Identify the four stages from the arrows: left side volume constant at $2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$, top side pressure constant at $1.5 \times 10^{5} \text{ Pa}$, right side volume constant at $5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$, bottom side pressure constant at $1.0 \times 10^{5} \text{ Pa}$.
State the rule: work $W = p\Delta V$ only when volume changes. Vertical lines have $\Delta V = 0$ so $W = 0$.

Follow the loop: the top stage goes from $2$ to $5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$, so volume increases and work is done by the gas. The bottom stage goes from $5$ to $2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$, so volume decreases and work is done on the gas.
Calculate the compression work: $p = 1.0 \times 10^{5} \text{ Pa}$ and $\Delta V = (5.0 - 2.0) \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3} = 3.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$.
Substitute: $W = (1.0 \times 10^{5}) \times (3.0 \times 10^{-4}) = 30 \text{ J}$. The unit $\text{Pa m}^{3}$ is $\text{J}$. This is option C.
